long_biography.plain_text:
Growing up beside Singapore's working port in Pasir Panjang gave Arthur Tay an early view of both trade and the sea. He accompanied his father, Tay Choon Hye, through the family ship-chandelling business and later recognised the demand for high-quality berthing in Asia. That insight led him to tender for Sentosa Cove and open ONE°15 Marina in 2007, despite early doubts about the market.

Tay has since taken the marina brand beyond Singapore while keeping SUTL's consumer-goods network at the centre of the wider group. His public work also extends to kidney care and ocean conservation. He continued his father's support for the National Kidney Foundation and helped fund an upgraded dialysis centre. In 2022 he launched Blue Water EduFest, a forum bringing together marine science, policy and industry.
long_biography.html:
Growing up beside Singapore's working port in Pasir Panjang gave Arthur Tay an early view of both trade and the sea. He accompanied his father, Tay Choon Hye, through the family ship-chandelling business and later recognised the demand for high-quality berthing in Asia. That insight led him to tender for Sentosa Cove and open ONE°15 Marina in 2007, despite early doubts about the market.

Tay has since taken the marina brand beyond Singapore while keeping SUTL's consumer-goods network at the centre of the wider group. His public work also extends to kidney care and ocean conservation. He continued his father's support for the National Kidney Foundation and helped fund an upgraded dialysis centre. In 2022 he launched Blue Water EduFest, a forum bringing together marine science, policy and industry.

uncertainties.detail: Official history records Tay's succession to his father, and filings show a sibling-owned family group with Arthur as controlling shareholder. Public sources do not disclose the exact estate distribution, the percentage he inherited or any later family transfers, so the classification does not claim a quantified inheritance.

Tay's private controlling interest spans consumer distribution, leisure, marinas, lifestyle brands and environmental services. Listed-company disclosures value the marina arm but do not supply a comparable valuation of the private consumer business, so Diversified is used instead of asserting that one segment dominates his current wealth.

A 2017 filing described Tay as aged 61 and a 2026 newspaper profile described him as 70, pointing to approximately 1956. Neither source establishes the exact birthday with enough precision, so no birth day, month, year, place or country is proposed.

A same-name Singapore LinkedIn account has an MBA-era recommendation and logistics references but is not publicly linked to SUTL, while another prominent namesake works in finance. No LinkedIn, Instagram or personal website met the identity threshold. Only the official SUTL company website is proposed.
Exact-name, company-name and site-specific Forbes searches found no dedicated Forbes profile for the Singaporean SUTL chairman. Similar-name business profiles were rejected.

The Citi direct profile independently states that Tay owns Hye Seas II and explains the name's link to his father, resolving the source record above the required threshold. This private context is excluded from both biographies and all wealth classifications.

Maritime tourism captures Tay's defining marina-development and operating mandate, while Marine / ocean conservation captures a separate institution-building commitment through Blue Water EduFest. No consumer-distribution tag was added because the active catalogue lacks a precise match and Multi-brand retail would overstate a distributor's direct retail model.
